title: Lower bound for a ratio of binomial coefficients
statement:
Let $n$, $\ell$, and $q$ be natural numbers with $n \ge 1$ and $q \ge 1$, and suppose that $q \le \ell$, $2\ell \le n$, and $2q \le n$. Then
\[
  e^{-3q}\left(\frac{\ell}{n}\right)^{q} \ \le\ \frac{\binom{n-2q}{\ell-q}}{\binom{n}{\ell}},
\]
where the binomial coefficients are evaluated in $\bbr$.
replaced:
Fact 4.2 (lower half).  Under the same hypotheses $n > 0$, $q > 0$, $q \le \ell$,
$2\ell \le n$ and $2q \le n$,
\[
  e^{-3q}\left(\frac{\ell}{n}\right)^{q} \ \le\ \frac{\binom{n-2q}{\ell-q}}{\binom{n}{\ell}},
\]
with the binomial coefficients again read in $\bbr$ via $\texttt{chooseR}$.
